definition: In computer graphics, view synthesis, or novel view synthesis, is a task which consists of generating images of a specific subject or scene from a specific point of view, when the only available information is pictures taken from different points of view.
details: This task was only recently (late 2010s – early 2020s) tackled with significant success, mostly as a result of advances in machine learning. Notable successful methods are Neural radiance fields and 3D Gaussian Splatting. Applications of view synthesis are numerous, one of them being Free view point television. The technique has also been applied to real-estate marketing, where novel views of a listing's interior are generated from a limited set of photographs for use in virtual home staging.

explainer.lead: View synthesis generates images of a subject or scene from a chosen viewpoint when only pictures from other viewpoints are available. It matters because it lets a small set of photos stand in for a full 3D capture.

tiers.eli5: It's like walking around a photo of a room and seeing the parts the photographer never shot.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers reconstruct a scene representation from a set of images and render novel viewpoints from it, using methods such as neural radiance fields or 3D Gaussian Splatting. A common pitfall is that views far from the captured angles degrade, since the scene is only constrained where images exist.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, given images from different points of view, generate an image of the same subject or scene from a specified new point of view; the task was tackled with significant success only in the late 2010s–early 2020s, mostly through machine learning. Limits: accuracy falls for viewpoints poorly covered by the input images.

explainer.example: A handful of interior photos of a house are used to synthesize new angles for virtual staging in a real-estate listing.
